title: Feedback
description: Response messages shown to learners after an action — correct, incorrect, hint, and encouragement. Culturally the most sensitive content type: tone of failure and success varies significantly across cultures.

language.description: BCP-47 language tag. Examples: en, it, de, es-419, nl-BE

feedbackType.description: The moment this feedback appears in the learning flow

formality.description: Register of address toward the learner. Must match the formality setting of the associated lesson and question.

sourceLanguage.description: BCP-47 tag of the language this was adapted from. Omit if this is the source.

sourceId.description: ID of the source feedback this was adapted from

relatedQuestion.description: ID of the question this feedback belongs to, if specific

primary.description: The main feedback message. Keep under 25 words. Must be actionable or affirming — never just 'Wrong.'

secondary.description: Optional follow-up shown below primary. Explains the why or offers the next step.

toneIntent.description: The intended emotional register. Required. Cultural reviewers must confirm this tone is appropriate in the target language before translation proceeds.

culturalNotes.description: Required when highCulturalRisk is true. Explicit notes about tone assumptions and what must change per locale.

avoidIn.description: Language codes where this exact message must NOT be used as-is. Triggers a full cultural rewrite instead of translation.

localizationFlags.description: Required on every content item. Signals content adaptability before translation begins.

highCulturalRisk.description: True when tone or idiom is likely to misfire in a different cultural context. When true, content.culturalNotes is required.

culturalReadinessScore.description: Assigned after completing the universal checklist.

if.description: When highCulturalRisk is true, content.culturalNotes is required.

content.primary: Exactly right. The denominator tells you the total number of parts.
content.culturalNotes: Neutral, informative tone. Safe for adaptation into all six target languages with minimal adjustment.

content.primary: Not quite. Take another look at which number is on the bottom.
content.secondary: Remember: the denominator is always the bottom number of the fraction.
content.culturalNotes: Original draft used an exclamation mark ('Not quite!'). Removed after cultural review — exclamation marks used for encouragement can read as condescending in DE/NL and overly casual in SV. The neutral version here transfers safely to all six target languages.
